subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should session archive/rotation become a first-class cron event trigger, a narrower plugin SDK/lifecycle hook, or remain plugin-owned without core cron config?
rationale: The source has the lifecycle signal and cron machinery, but binding them creates a new public automation/config/security contract around session metadata and durable event dispatch.

options.title: Design core cron event trigger
options.body: Add a durable, scoped session lifecycle event schedule to cron with permission checks, dedupe, and trace records before exposing it in config or CLI.

options.title: Expose plugin-owned hook only
options.body: Keep core cron unchanged and document a plugin/SDK pattern that lets memory or automation plugins handle `session_end` without a public cron event surface.

options.title: Defer lifecycle automation
options.body: Leave the current polling/new-session workaround as the supported path until a broader automation event bus design is approved.

recommendation.title: Design core cron event trigger
recommendation.body: Add a durable, scoped session lifecycle event schedule to cron with permission checks, dedupe, and trace records before exposing it in config or CLI.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame points to the central session and cron contracts in dongdong's recent commit, making this the best available routing candidate from local history.
